event.title: The God of the Operating Room
event.announcement: After two absurd operating-room mishaps in a row, Kaori quietly starts deferring primary-surgeon slots—until an off-duty "empirical control observation" in empty OR #3 collides head-on with a real surgical abdomen.
event.completion_hint: Kaori Miyama's Relationship has reached Lv3 — "Even when I started doubting my own judgment, you still dared to put the primary surgeon's scalpel back in my hands."

choices.s08_013:a: "You take lead. Let Sayaka hold the table for two minutes while I throw on scrubs and scrub in as your first assistant—I'm backing you."
choices.s08_013:b: "You verified her identity, the perforation on CT, and the surgical indication yourself. Take the primary spot; I'll stand across from you to watch exposure and double-check."
choices.s08_013:c: "Your team and backup are all right here—no need to second-guess yourself. Run it on your emergency judgment, and leave first assist to me."
choices.s10c_002:a: "I'll keep traction tension strictly within safe limits—let's open up the lateral plane right along the gallbladder wall first."
choices.s10c_002:b: "The local edema and oozing are clouding the field—let me gently suction-dissect first to clear the inferior margin of Hartmann's pouch."
choices.s10e_003:a: "Are you thinking of that faint, blurry fluid shadow along the right paracolic gutter on the pre-op CT?"
choices.s10e_003:b: "The emptied gallbladder volume and the subhepatic fluid really don't add up. Are you planning to check lower down, or worried about disturbing the bowel?"
choices.s12_016:a: "The outcome proved my judgment right—nobody else tonight might have caught that pocket down in the right paracolic gutter."
choices.s12_016:b: "If I'd snatched your scalpel back there, you'd be marching up to me with the chart tomorrow morning to lecture me for half a month."
choices.s12_016:c: "We weathered the first two mix-ups on opposite sides of the same table—it's about time we finally got to see a real emergency surgery through properly together."

nodes.s02_001: At five-forty in the evening, outpatient clinics and daytime ward rounds were wrapping up one after another, and the evening breeze on the rooftop blew away the lingering scent of antiseptic.
nodes.s02_002: Ryuji Sakaguchi had just pushed open the heavy iron rooftop door for a breath of fresh air when he spotted Kaori Miyama standing by the western railing. She held an ER observation clipboard with its transfer note already signed, gazing evenly down at the ambulance lane outside the hospital gates.
nodes.s02_003: Hearing footsteps, Miyama glanced back over her shoulder and gave a natural nod.
nodes.s02_005: "Just finished entering the post-op orders for this afternoon's hernia repair. What about you? Passing the first-floor ER triage desk earlier, I heard the nurses say you sorted out three fevers of unknown origin and an upper GI bleed in half an hour—on a hot streak today?"
nodes.s02_006: Miyama cracked open the can of black coffee in her hand and took a sip, her tone as crisp and matter-of-fact as ever.
nodes.s02_007: "The symptoms and lab slips are right there on paper. Triaging by urgency is simply what emergency medicine is supposed to do—luck has nothing to do with it."
nodes.s02_008: Sakaguchi walked over to the railing beside her and paused, glancing at the clipboard in her hand.
nodes.s02_009: "That acute appendicitis admitted at four o'clock—you did the initial workup and physical exam yourself, didn't you? On the OR board, Sayaka's name was listed as primary surgeon."
nodes.s02_010: Miyama's fingers paused ever so slightly against the coffee can, her gaze remaining fixed on the distant streetscape.
nodes.s02_011: "Dr. Nanjo happened to walk past the ER after finishing her clinic, so I handed the lead spot over to her. Staying downstairs to watch the other two observation beds keeps turnover moving faster."
nodes.s02_012: There wasn't a single flaw in her reasoning; if anything, it sounded even more methodical than usual. Yet the Kaori Miyama of just a short while ago—who would read a plain film in the ER and decisively call for an OR setup on the spot—would never have gone out of her way to pass off a clear-cut acute abdomen like that.
nodes.s02_013: Sakaguchi didn't call her on it, simply offering an offhand remark.
nodes.s02_014: "Here I thought you'd just open it yourself and page me to scrub in as first assistant."
nodes.s02_015: Miyama shot him a sidelong glance, one brow arching slightly as the corner of her mouth tugged into a dry, half-wry curve.
nodes.s02_016: "What, has Dr. Sakaguchi got too much free time lately? Helping me write that dictionary-thick wrong-patient laparotomy incident report last week didn't drain all the ink out of your pen?"
nodes.s02_017: "It was a lot of pages, sure, but sorting out the workflow loopholes meant it wasn't written for nothing."
nodes.s02_018: "Yeah. The workflow loopholes are sorted out."
nodes.s02_019: The evening breeze brushed past her neat purple hair. Looking down at the small metal pull-tab on the rim of the can, her voice flattened by a shade—devoid of self-pity, sounding instead as though she were calmly examining an equation she hadn't quite solved yet.
nodes.s02_020: "While organizing ER follow-ups the past couple of days, I kept thinking—if your suturing or knot-tying isn't clean enough, you can practice on a silicone pad a hundred times after shift until your hands get it right. Clinical judgment isn't like that. Once the decision to wheel a patient into the OR starts off skewed, standing under the shadowless lamp leaves you nowhere to pretend nothing happened."
nodes.s02_022: "I'm not fixating on it. Those two cases didn't even share the same root cause—I can tell that much pathology and logic apart."
nodes.s02_023: Tilting her chin up, she finished the last bitter sip of black coffee and tossed the empty can cleanly into the recycling bin beside them.
nodes.s02_024: "It's just that both of my parents spent their whole lives as sharp, clear-headed physicians. Growing up hearing them debate difficult cases across the dinner table, I've seen more than enough brilliant doctors. Now that I'm wearing this coat inside a hospital myself, I don't care to have people think highly of me because of my surname—and I have even less intention of turning into some half-baked surgeon who talks big about decisiveness while making a farce out of the operating table every time."
nodes.s02_025: She clipped her observation chart back together and turned toward Sakaguchi, her expression already restored to its usual poised crispness.
nodes.s02_026: "All right, that's enough fresh air—I'm heading back down to hand off the evening ER shift. Tomorrow's my rotation day off. I already annotated the morning interdepartmental consult slips and left them on your desk. If you can't read my shorthand, just text me instead of guessing."
nodes.s02_027: "Your handwriting's way easier to read than Chief Mizuki's, Dr. Miyama. Go enjoy your day off."
nodes.s02_028: Miyama gave a light huff, the corner of her mouth curving almost imperceptibly before she turned and pushed open the stairwell door.
nodes.s03_001: At ten-thirty the next morning, Ryuji Sakaguchi walked up to the nurses' station counter carrying two postoperative suture-removal appointment slips.
nodes.s03_002: Hiroko Sugimura took the slips, briskly verified the bed numbers, and flipped open the surgical department's weekly scheduling ledger beside her to file them. When she turned to the ER-liaison page, the tip of her pen paused, and she let out a quiet sigh.
nodes.s03_003: "Come to think of it, Dr. Miyama's ER transfer notes this week are just as crystal-clear as ever—even the antibiotic skin-test timestamps are marked down to the minute... Only she's left the primary-surgeon column blank for General Surgery to fill in four or five days straight now."
nodes.s03_004: Sakaguchi's pen paused mid-signature as he looked up at Hiroko.
nodes.s03_005: "Nursing noticed it too? Here I half-wondered if the hospital had temporarily restricted her primary-surgeon privileges after the conference-room debrief."
nodes.s03_006: Hiroko shook her head, lowering her voice just enough for the two of them at the counter.
nodes.s03_007: "Nothing of the sort—neither Director Shiromiya nor Nurse Manager Ishigami suspended her operating privileges. Yesterday an urgent trauma debridement came into the ER, and Dr. Miyama controlled the bleeders right there in the treatment bay in no time flat, steady as a rock. Yet the moment a case requires going up to the OR to open an abdomen, she prepares every pre-op workup and chart summary impeccably—and then steps back to assistant or consult right when it's time to sign as primary."
nodes.s03_008: Half-closing the ledger, Hiroko wore a rare look somewhere between gentle amusement and subtle puzzlement.
nodes.s03_009: "And the evening before last at shift change, I happened to drop off a supply sheet at the Nursing Office and walked right into something pretty unusual at the door—you've known Dr. Miyama long enough to know how much she hates superstitious talk, right, Dr. Sakaguchi?"
nodes.s03_010: "She thinks even saying 'hope it's a quiet night shift' lacks scientific rigor. What was she seeing Nurse Manager Ishigami about?"
nodes.s03_011: "She was standing right in front of the nursing director's desk with a dead-serious look on her face, asking Nurse Manager Ishigami whether—in all her years on the job—she had ever run into a stretch where 'you follow standard protocol to the letter, yet still collide with one low-probability freak incident after another.'"
nodes.s03_013: "How did Nurse Manager Ishigami answer her?"
nodes.s03_014: "I fully expected her to tell Dr. Miyama to go reread the safety manual. Instead, Nurse Manager Ishigami didn't even set down her roster—just looked up at her for two seconds and said two plain sentences: 'A place like a hospital carries its own currents of air. When you hit a threshold you can't get past, dodging it won't help—you have to step across it yourself.'"
nodes.s03_016: "...Nurse Manager Ishigami actually said that herself?"
nodes.s03_017: "Every word—I heard it clear as day by the doorway. Right afterward, of course, she tacked on her usual by-the-book 'Go catch up on your sleep and stop overthinking in the corridors.' Except when Dr. Miyama heard the first half, she nodded thoughtfully as if she'd suddenly seized on a research hypothesis and walked right out."
nodes.s03_018: Smiling wryly, Hiroko handed the verified suture-removal receipt back to Sakaguchi.
nodes.s03_019: "Dr. Miyama acts tougher than anyone on the surface, when in truth she's taking those first two incidents harder than anyone else. Today's supposed to be her day off—I just hope she's home getting a proper sleep instead of brooding over strange ideas by herself."
nodes.s03_020: Taking the receipt, Sakaguchi recalled Miyama's guarded words on the rooftop the evening before, a faint sense of unease stirring in his chest.
nodes.s03_021: "I need to drop off a signature folder in the administrative wing this afternoon anyway—I'll stop by the Director's Office and ask."
nodes.s04_001: At four thirty-five in the afternoon, the administrative corridor was hushed.
nodes.s04_002: Carrying the approval folder up to the Director's Office, Ryuji Sakaguchi had just raised his right hand to knock when he noticed the heavy wooden door wasn't latched shut, leaving a finger-width gap.
nodes.s04_003: Two unmistakably familiar women's voices drifted from inside—one of them belonging to Kaori Miyama, who was supposed to be off duty today. Sakaguchi's raised hand froze mid-air.
nodes.s04_004: Kaori Miyama (inside the room, her tone as calm as a morning-conference case presentation):
nodes.s04_005: "First time, we opened the abdomen and found the patient completely healthy; second time, we opened the abdomen and found the person on the table wasn't even the patient. Two consecutive deviations of that magnitude from the primary seat or lead decision-maker can no longer be brushed aside as statistical coincidence."
nodes.s04_006: Asuka Shiromiya (inside the room, accompanied by the crisp click of a fountain-pen cap snapping shut):
nodes.s04_007: "Kaori, let me remind you one more time: you graduated with honors from medical university and you are an emergency physician. No exorcisms in my hospital."
nodes.s04_008: Kaori Miyama (inside the room, objecting seriously):
nodes.s04_009: "This isn't superstition, Asuka—it's empirical elimination. Chart verification, instrument workflow, and staff handoffs have all been audited item by item in our review report. The sole environmental confounding variable I haven't personally verified from the opposite perspective is the operating room itself."
nodes.s04_011: "Wrapping wild overthinking in experimental terminology doesn't magically make it scientific. Today is your rotation day off. I only cleared you to come in so you could sign last week's leftover supply slips—finish signing them and go straight home to sleep—"
nodes.s04_012: With a crisp click, the Director's Office door was pulled open from within.
nodes.s04_013: Kaori Miyama, just stepping out, came face-to-face with Ryuji Sakaguchi standing a pace away with his knuckles still poised in mid-air.
nodes.s04_014: Silence hung in the air for a full second.
nodes.s04_015: Normally unflappable, Miyama stiffened almost imperceptibly at the tips of her ears, clearly not expecting anyone outside the door. Yet within half a second she tamped down that flash of awkwardness, straightened her spine ramrod-tall, and resumed her usual sharp, composed bearing.
nodes.s04_016: "...Dr. Sakaguchi. Here for the Director's signature?"
nodes.s04_017: "Yeah, dropping off next week's specialty schedule. Isn't today your day off?"
nodes.s04_018: "Just swung by to catch up on a couple of administrative signatures. I was just leaving."
nodes.s04_019: Giving Sakaguchi a polite, restrained nod that left zero opening to ask about 'empirical elimination,' she strode crisply down the hall—except a closer look showed she hadn't turned toward the main lobby elevators, but toward the skybridge leading back to the inpatient and surgical floors.
nodes.s04_020: Behind her desk, Asuka Shiromiya watched her old classmate's retreating back, rubbed helplessly between her brows, and waved Sakaguchi inside.
nodes.s04_021: "Come on in, Dr. Sakaguchi—no need to stand guard in the doorway. You caught the tail end of that just now, didn't you?"
nodes.s04_022: Sakaguchi stepped into the office and set the schedule folder on her desk.
nodes.s04_023: "Only the last couple of lines about 'exorcism' and 'empirical elimination.' Is that why she's been passing off primary-surgeon slots down in the ER all week?"
nodes.s04_024: Flipping through the folder to sign it, Asuka let some of her directorial formality drop, revealing genuine concern for a lifelong friend.
nodes.s04_025: "She's had that single-minded streak since we were students. The more logical someone is—and the higher the bar they set for their own clinical judgment—the harder it is to brush past running headfirst into two operating-table mishaps that read like dark comedy no matter how you explain them."
nodes.s04_026: Handing the signed folder back to Sakaguchi, Asuka met his eyes earnestly.
nodes.s04_027: "There is nothing whatsoever wrong with her emergency judgment or surgical technique—nobody knows that better than I do. Still, as hospital director I can't force her onto the primary spot by administrative order, and as an old classmate she writes off anything reassuring I say as polite lip service. Dr. Sakaguchi, you stood right beside her through both of those cases—if the right moment comes up around the hospital, talk to her as her surgical partner, would you?"
nodes.s04_028: "Understood. Though when she left just now, she didn't head toward the front entrance—she took the skybridge toward the surgical wing."
nodes.s04_029: Asuka paused, glancing up at the wall clock.
nodes.s04_030: "Toward the surgical wing? Today's elective list finished wrapping up at four-thirty—only OR #1 still has an emergency vascular trauma running, so Rooms #2 and #3 should both be empty right now... Surely she wouldn't actually go into an operating room to inspect 'environmental variables'?"
nodes.s04_031: "I need to pick up an instrument request form up on the fourth-floor OR suite anyway. I'll swing by and check."
nodes.s04_032: "Good—let me sign off on this monthly report and I'll head right up too!"
nodes.s05_001: At five-oh-five in the evening, the fourth-floor surgical corridor was quiet enough to hear the faint whisper of airflow through the ventilation ducts.
nodes.s05_002: Outside OR #1, the red 'IN SURGERY' lamp glowed steadily; yet down at the far end of the hall, where OR #3 should have been completely idle, a sliver of overhead light spilled through the unlatched sensor door.
nodes.s05_003: Stopping outside OR #3, Ryuji Sakaguchi pressed the touch plate and stepped inside.
nodes.s05_004: Two paces into the outer aisle, Sakaguchi stopped dead in his tracks.
nodes.s05_005: In the middle of the empty operating room, lit only by a single bank of standard prep lights, young nurse Moe Honjo stood clutching a laundry basket of folded street clothes in utter, fidgeting panic—while stretched out flat on her back atop the narrow operating table Kaori Miyama knew so well lay a young woman without a stitch of clothing on, wearing nothing at all save a disposable blue bouffant surgical cap, both wrists and ankles neatly fastened into the quick-release safety restraint straps along the sides.
nodes.s05_006: It wasn't an inpatient who had wandered into the wrong room.
nodes.s05_007: Beneath the surgical cap, that poised, coolly sculpted face belonged unmistakably to off-duty emergency physician Kaori Miyama. Worse still, under the quiet, cool overhead lights, her eyes were peacefully shut and her breathing slow and even—she had fallen fast asleep right there on the operating table.
nodes.s05_008: Looking up to see Sakaguchi walk in, Moe Honjo nearly jumped out of her skin, waving both hands frantically in a hushed whisper.
nodes.s05_009: "D-Dr. Sakaguchi?! Please don't get the wrong idea!! I swear I wasn't the one who tied Dr. Miyama to the table!!"
nodes.s05_010: Pointing at the neatly folded casual clothes in the basket, Moe looked half a breath from tears as she whispered a report of the most absurd ten minutes of her nursing career.
nodes.s05_011: "Twenty minutes ago Dr. Miyama suddenly flagged me down outside by herself and declared with a completely straight face that she needed to run a 'non-anesthetized, non-invasive patient-position empirical variable elimination' in an empty OR! She stripped off every piece of her own clothes and put them in the basket herself, put the cap on herself, climbed onto the table herself... She insisted that unless her wrists and ankles were buckled to pre-op standards with a nurse standing watch, the experimental control conditions wouldn't be rigorous! I triple-checked that these are the one-pull quick-release safety straps—and less than three minutes after I clicked them shut, Dr. Miyama closed her eyes thinking about something, her breathing slowed down, and she fell straight asleep...!"
nodes.s05_012: A nerve twitched faintly at Sakaguchi's temple as he walked up beside the operating table and looked down.
nodes.s05_013: Exhausted from nights of incident reviews piled atop back-to-back ER shifts, Kaori Miyama still held the faintest furrow between her brows even fast asleep on the firm table pad.
nodes.s05_015: On the table, Miyama's eyelashes fluttered twice before her eyes slowly opened.
nodes.s05_016: For the first second, she stared up in groggy haze at the unlit dome of the shadowless lamp overhead; the next second, turning her head to register Sakaguchi standing beside the table, she glanced down at her completely uncovered body and her wrists buckled to the armboards.
nodes.s05_017: A faint flush rose instantly from the base of her pale ears down to her collarbones. Dead silence gripped the operating room for two full seconds.
nodes.s05_019: Miyama closed her eyes once; when she opened them again, sheer willpower forced every trace of discomfiture off her face as she delivered a single word in the flat cadence of a clinical research briefing:
nodes.s05_022: "Eliminating anomalous variables in the OR environment and patient-side perspective. Given two consecutive inexplicable deviations while standing in the surgeon's position, conducting a control observation from the opposite side of the table is a reasonable step."
nodes.s05_023: "So coming into the hospital on your day off, stripping naked, and strapping yourself onto an empty operating table counts as a control observation?"
nodes.s05_024: Kaori Miyama (turning her head half an inch aside, her tone still deadpan serious):
nodes.s05_025: "Without reproducing baseline patient conditions, the control would be incomplete. And strictly speaking—the trial has not concluded yet, so I haven't reached a final conclusion."
nodes.s05_027: Miyama stalled for half a second, the tips of her ears turning a shade redder before she shot back stiffly:
nodes.s05_028: "...That was incidental. I simply stayed up late reading journals last night; it has no bearing on the trial itself."
nodes.s06_001: Before the last syllable had even faded, the automatic door of OR #3 slid open with another crisp swoosh.
nodes.s06_002: Having just signed her monthly report and hurried up to the fourth floor, Asuka Shiromiya stepped briskly inside:
nodes.s06_003: "Dr. Sakaguchi, have you found Kaori ye—"
nodes.s06_004: The last word lodged straight in the young director's throat.
nodes.s06_005: Stopping three paces from the foot of the table, Asuka let her gaze travel slowly from a trembling Moe Honjo to her longtime medical-school best friend lying stark naked in a blue elastic surgical cap with both wrists and ankles neatly buckled into the safety straps.
nodes.s06_006: After a three-second silence that stretched on like a century, Asuka slowly raised one hand to press against her forehead and closed her eyes.
nodes.s06_009: "Yesterday afternoon, and again half an hour ago in my office, I told you twice—no exorcisms in my hospital."
nodes.s06_010: "I told you it's not superstition, Asuka. It's empirical elimination. Even Nurse Manager Ishigami said a hospital's atmosphere is tied to one's position and you have to step across a threshold yourself—I was simply verifying the variable of 'lying on the table' rigorously—"
nodes.s06_011: Asuka Shiromiya (opening her eyes and cutting in expressionlessly):
nodes.s06_012: "Ishigami meant stop dodging primary-surgeon shifts, not strip naked on your day off to nap on Table Three. This isn't empirical elimination—it's sleep-deprived performance art."
nodes.s06_013: "I haven't written the conclusion yet, so it doesn't qualify as performance art."
nodes.s06_014: "And you are NOT writing it into any report!"
nodes.s06_015: Drawing a deep breath to tamp down her exasperation with her old classmate, Asuka remembered her duty as director and turned seriously toward Moe Honjo beside the table.
nodes.s06_016: "Nurse Honjo, even at Dr. Miyama's personal request, occupying a standby OR without clinical orders for a private experiment is against protocol. Don't let it happen again—unbuckle the safety straps right away and let her get dressed."
nodes.s06_017: Moe Honjo (nodding rapidly in sheer relief):
nodes.s06_018: "Y-Yes, Director! Dr. Miyama, I'll unfasten you right now—"
nodes.s07_001: Moe Honjo's fingers had barely brushed the left armboard's quick-release buckle when the doors of OR #3 burst open from outside!
nodes.s07_002: Clutching a stack of freshly printed contrast abdominal CT films and an emergency admission checklist tight against her chest, OR nurse Ange Tonegawa reported at rapid-fire speed without slurring a syllable:
nodes.s07_003: "Director! Dr. Sakaguchi! Crash surgical patient coming straight up the ER green channel—twenty-three-year-old young female patient Kasumi Asou, complicated acute cholecystitis with gallbladder perforation and biliary peritonitis! She's conscious and alert, dual-source ID verification is completed at both the ER and OR entrance, and they're transferring her onto the table next door in OR #2 right now! Chief Mido's severe vascular trauma in Room #1 is still in the middle of an anastomosis and can't break scrub—the only surgeon on deck right now is Dr. Nanjo receiving her in Room #2!"
nodes.s07_004: In the exact instant the words 'gallbladder perforation, biliary peritonitis' hit her ears—
nodes.s07_005: Every trace of embarrassment and blush vanished from Kaori Miyama's face within a tenth of a second. Her burgundy eyes turned razor-calm and incisive, snapping straight back into the ER trauma physician whose reflexes cut like a scalpel.
nodes.s07_006: "Honjo, release the straps! Ange, give me her latest vitals, perforation site on imaging, and broad-spectrum antibiotic infusion time—talk while we move!"
nodes.s07_007: With two crisp clicks, Moe Honjo yanked open the quick-release buckles on both sides and snatched up the folded casual clothes from the basket:
nodes.s07_009: But Ange's next line of report was already coming fast on its heels:
nodes.s07_010: "Temperature thirty-eight-nine, heart rate one-twelve, blood pressure one-oh-two over sixty-four, marked right upper quadrant and right-sided tenderness with rebound! Cefoperazone-sulbactam started IV in the ER ten minutes ago—"
nodes.s07_011: Hearing that her blood pressure was already flirting with a borderline drop, Miyama vaulted off the table, spared one glance at her casual clothes that would cost precious seconds to pull on, and didn't waste even ten seconds dressing—without even taking off the patient bouffant cap already tucking in every strand of her purple hair, she snatched a tie-on surgical mask off the connecting prep counter, tied it securely on the move, and sprinted barefoot straight into OR #2 next door!
nodes.s07_012: Sakaguchi and Asuka hurried out of Room #3 right behind her, stepping into the outer observation perimeter of OR #2.
nodes.s07_013: Inside OR #2, twenty-three-year-old female patient Kasumi Asou had just been transferred onto the table with baseline monitors attached and had not yet undergone general anesthesia induction, while Sayaka Nanjo stood tableside verifying pre-op readiness.
nodes.s07_014: Hurrying into the outer non-sterile perimeter, Miyama halted strictly two meters clear of the yellow line and sterile instrument tables, not letting so much as half a fingertip near anything sterile. Wearing nothing whatsoever save the bouffant cap already on her head and the surgical mask she had just tied on, she caught the eye of the patient on the table—who froze solid and stared wide-eyed toward the doorway:
nodes.s07_016: "W-Wait a second...?! Doctor, Nurse... w-why did a naked woman just run into the operating room over there?! Wearing nothing but a cap and a mask... Am I burning up so badly I'm hallucinating?!"
nodes.s07_017: Completely locked into emergency resuscitation mode with her eyes fixed on the live vital-signs monitor and the abdominal CT on the lightbox, Miyama didn't spare a half-second to explain, firing off deployment orders rapid and crystal-clear:
nodes.s07_018: "Ange, read back to me independently the full name, date of birth, and allergy history the patient stated in her own words, and verify fluid resuscitation drip rate! Honjo, pull an open cholecystectomy tray, deep abdominal Poole suction, and warm saline irrigation set from Sterile Cabinet Two immediately! Sayaka, hold pre-op prep steady at the table for a moment!"
nodes.s07_019: "Yes, Doctor! Patient's spoken name, date of birth, and dual outpatient-ER wristbands match one hundred percent, no known drug allergies, and a second large-bore IV line is wide open!"
nodes.s07_020: Seeing Miyama wholly absorbed in cross-checking the CT films and fluid resuscitation pace, Sakaguchi quickly donned a disposable cap, surgical mask, and exam gloves at the entrance prep station, stepped briskly to the head of the table, and picked up the pre-oxygenation mask to reassure the patient gently:
nodes.s07_021: "Easy now—don't mind the commotion over in the prep area; the whole surgical team is getting everything ready for you as fast as possible. I'm Dr. Sakaguchi, assisting on your surgery, and I'm going to start your general anesthesia now. Take nice, deep breaths into the mask for me."
nodes.s07_022: Sakaguchi steadily administered the intravenous induction agents while holding the mask seal for assisted oxygenation. As the patient's breathing slowed and her heavy eyelids drifted shut, she murmured sleepily beneath the mask right before losing consciousness:
nodes.s07_023: "Mmm... how strange... if she's just a high-fever hallucination... why are her orders so professional..."
nodes.s07_024: Once the patient was smoothly under general anesthesia, Sakaguchi secured the airway, verified ventilation parameters with Ange, and looked up to exchange a glance with Asuka Shiromiya by the doorway—this time, the patient's identity was beyond doubt, the surgical abdomen was rock-solid, and not half a minute could be wasted.
nodes.s08_001: Having confirmed that induction was stable, fluid resuscitation was holding systolic pressure steady inside Room #2, and Sayaka Nanjo was already leading pre-incision skin prep, Miyama and Sakaguchi stepped back out to the scrub sinks.
nodes.s08_002: Warm water gushed from the sensor faucet with a soft rush.
nodes.s08_003: Reaching both hands out toward the antimicrobial scrub dispenser, Miyama abruptly froze mid-motion for half a second. She glanced through the viewing window at the patient being draped inside, then turned toward Sakaguchi and Asuka beside her, her voice pitched low beneath her mask:
nodes.s08_004: "...Sakaguchi's in the hospital today. Let Sakaguchi take primary on this one—or let Sayaka lead directly, and I'll scrub in as assistant."
nodes.s08_005: Asuka Shiromiya stood beside the scrub sink, looking at her calmly:
nodes.s08_007: At her sides, Miyama's fingers curled slightly tighter. Without dramatics or self-pity, she spoke plainly as a physician accountable for a patient's life, laying bare the hesitation weighing on her:
nodes.s08_008: "You know why, Asuka. Last month we opened up someone who wasn't even sick, and last week I opened the wrong person from the primary spot. Lying in there today is a textbook gallbladder perforation with biliary peritonitis—if my intraoperative judgment slips again, spreading sepsis isn't something an incident report can clean up. There's no need to gamble by putting me in the lead seat."
nodes.s08_009: Meeting her best friend's taut gaze, Asuka offered no cheap platitudes, instead laying out the objective facts point by point as Director of Hoshimi Hospital:
nodes.s08_010: "Her dual-source identity, fever and white-count labs, the gallbladder wall defect on CT, and the free fluid signs—you verified every single one of those with your own eyes just now. Emergency open cholecystectomy and source control sit squarely within your credentialed operating privileges, and both Sayaka and Dr. Sakaguchi are right here scrubbing in alongside you."
nodes.s08_011: Pausing briefly, Asuka spoke with clear, unwavering conviction:
nodes.s08_012: "All I know is that neither of the first two cases proved you don't know how to operate—and they are certainly no reason to step back when an emergency patient genuinely needs you."
nodes.s08_013: Her breath catching faintly, Miyama glanced instinctively toward Sakaguchi as he unclipped his ID badge to scrub in.
nodes.s08_014: Without a moment's hesitation, Sakaguchi met her gaze squarely.
nodes.s08_015: "You take lead. Sayaka's holding the table inside—give me two minutes to throw on scrubs and scrub in, and I'll be right across from you as first assistant. I'm backing you, Miyama."
nodes.s08_016: Miyama blinked once; above her mask, her burgundy eyes held Sakaguchi's for two full seconds as the last trace of wavering quietly settled.
nodes.s08_017: "...You'd better mean that. Standing across the table from me leaves zero room to slack off."
nodes.s08_018: Sakaguchi gestured toward the contrast CT films hanging on the lightbox inside OR #2, his voice steady and grounded.
nodes.s08_019: "Her identity, the wall defect on imaging, and the surgical indication—you verified all of it firsthand from the very first minute. Nobody knows her condition right now better than you do. Take the primary spot; I'll change, scrub in, and stand across from you to watch exposure and double-check."
nodes.s08_020: Following his gesture to the crisp CT slices, Miyama let the tight furrow between her brows ease and gave a firm nod.
nodes.s08_021: "...Right. Both the films and clinical signs line up—there's nothing left to hesitate over."
nodes.s08_022: Sakaguchi spoke in a calm, measured voice.
nodes.s08_023: "Sayaka, Ange, and Honjo are all in position inside, and I'm scrubbing right in as your first assistant. Your team and backup are all here—just drive the case forward on your usual emergency judgment."
nodes.s08_024: Drawing a deep breath, Miyama let her gaze sharpen back to crystal clarity.
nodes.s08_025: "...All right. Having all of you watching the field beside me is more than enough."
nodes.s08_026: Watching her best friend step back onto the foot pedal of the scrub sink, Asuka let a faint smile of relief touch her lips.
nodes.s08_027: "Go on, Kaori. I'll be waiting outside for good news."
nodes.s08_028: "Right. Sakaguchi—make it quick and keep up!"
nodes.s09_001: Sakaguchi ducked into the adjacent doctors' locker room, changed into his green scrubs as fast as humanly possible, and squared away his surgical cap and tie-on mask.
nodes.s09_002: When he stepped back out to the scrub sinks, he was startled to find Miyama hadn't gone back to the women's locker room to hunt for clothes at all—still wearing nothing whatsoever save her bouffant cap and mask, she stood at the basin scrubbing meticulously from fingertips past both elbows strictly to sterile protocol, then held her dripping forearms high and toed open the automatic door of OR #2.
nodes.s09_003: Completing his own surgical scrub at top speed, Sakaguchi followed right behind her into OR #2.
nodes.s09_004: Walking straight up to the outer edge of the sterile back table, Miyama dried both forearms with a sterile towel and held her hands out toward the scrub nurse—where Moe Honjo, lifting an unfolded dark-green long-sleeved sterile surgical gown to present, froze solid on the spot the instant she got a clear look at Dr. Miyama, her eyes going wide as saucers.
nodes.s09_005: To preserve professional order inside the operating room, Moe swallowed her yelp by sheer willpower and held out the open sterile gown with trembling hands for Miyama to slip her arms into; on the circulating side, Ange Tonegawa blinked for half a beat before stepping briskly behind Miyama to draw the back panels together and secure the ties. Across the instrument table, Moe couldn't quite hold it in and whispered:
nodes.s09_006: "D-Dr. Miyama... a sterile surgical gown isn't meant to be worn as everyday clothing."
nodes.s09_007: Holding both arms level as she was gowned, her gaze already fixed past the sterile drapes onto the prepped right upper quadrant of the patient's abdomen, Miyama answered calmly:
nodes.s09_009: Moe Honjo (her fingers trembling faintly as she peeled open the sterile glove pack):
nodes.s09_010: "...Except what you're doing right now makes me seriously doubt whether you actually are!"
nodes.s09_011: "I'm off shift today without a spare set of scrubs staged, and going back to rummage through the locker room would waste precious minutes before incision. Cap, mask, surgical scrub, and full-length sterile gown—not a single step was skipped, the patient is already on the table, and the sterile zone runs across the chest and sleeves. Ange, cinch the back ties snug; Honjo, size-seven sterile gloves."
nodes.s09_012: Ange Tonegawa secured the back ties crisply and stepped back into the circulating zone; staring at Dr. Miyama—whose expression was so utterly solemn there wasn't room for a single stray thought—Moe gulped, let her OR-nurse instincts override every urge to protest, and held the sterile latex glove cuffs wide for her to plunge her hands cleanly inside:
nodes.s09_014: Across the room, having likewise been gowned and gloved with circulating assistance, Sakaguchi approached the operating table from behind and to the side of the primary surgeon's spot.
nodes.s09_015: Bright, cool beams from the overhead surgical lamp poured straight down onto the center of the table.
nodes.s09_016: Standing at the primary position, Miyama leaned slightly forward, her bouffant cap sealing in every lock of purple hair, her tie-on mask covering the lower half of her face, and her gloved hands resting steadily along the sterile drape margin as she studied the incision mark—Sayaka Nanjo holding retractors temporarily across from her, and Moe Honjo guarding the instrument stand at her side.
nodes.s09_017: Viewed purely from across or in front of the table, she looked every inch the composed, commanding, unimpeachable emergency attending surgeon; only from the three-quarter rear angle as Sakaguchi stepped up could one catch, between the overlapping back ties of the dark-green sterile gown, the unmistakable realization that there wasn't a thread on underneath.
nodes.s09_018: Yet the woman herself didn't so much as bat an eyelash. Sensing Sakaguchi step close, Miyama shifted her gaze half an inch with effortless composure:
nodes.s09_019: "Right on time, Sakaguchi. Relieve Sayaka across the table and take first assistant—stand by for final pre-incision check."
nodes.s10a_001: Sakaguchi took his place as first assistant while Sayaka Nanjo handed off the prepped field notes and shifted to the side as second assistant on retraction.
nodes.s10a_002: Moe Honjo already had the belly-blade scalpel poised at hand, yet rather than reaching for it right away, Miyama raised her eyes first toward Ange Tonegawa on the circulating side and the abdominal CT on the wall lightbox.
nodes.s10a_003: "One last team-wide independent closed-loop check before skin incision. Ange, read back the wristband, original ER intake sheet, and the timestamp and full name on these CT films one more time."
nodes.s10a_004: "Check complete! Kasumi Asou, twenty-three-year-old female—original ER intake record, bilateral wristbands, and our 16:58 contrast CT match one hundred percent on full name and chart number; general anesthesia and all vital monitors are stable, and broad-spectrum antibiotics have finished infusing."
nodes.s10a_005: Following Miyama's gaze, Sakaguchi scanned the abdominal CT on the lightbox as well—the gallbladder in the right upper quadrant was markedly distended with a distinct focal defect at the fundus and clear pericholecystic and subhepatic fluid; beyond that, further lateral and inferior along the margin of the right paracolic gutter lay a faint, wispy low-attenuation fluid streak hugging the bowel wall, impossible to tell from imaging alone whether it was true dependent tracking or merely artifact.
nodes.s10a_006: Satisfied that every primary source lined up seamlessly without the slightest ambiguity, Miyama held out her right hand steadily.
nodes.s10a_007: "Good. Right upper quadrant transrectus incision—Honjo, scalpel."
nodes.s10b_001: Her opening stroke parted skin and subcuticular tissue cleanly. Not a fraction of Miyama's technical fundamentals had dulled from her hesitation earlier that week—electrocautery hemostasis and layered entry moved briskly and surely, with Sakaguchi sponging in seamless rhythm across the table.
nodes.s10b_002: Yet the very instant the peritoneum parted and the abdominal cavity opened, a turbid gush of yellow-green bile mixed with fibrinous exudate welled straight into view.
nodes.s10b_003: At the exact same moment, the anesthesia monitor at the head of the table sounded two low warning chimes.
nodes.s10b_004: "Dr. Miyama, blood pressure dipped right after abdominal decompression—ninety-four over fifty-eight, heart rate up to one-eighteen!"
nodes.s10b_005: "Adhesions under the liver are pretty dense here—the gallbladder fundus has gone purplish-black, gangrenous, and perforated, with bilious exudate all around it."
nodes.s10b_006: Confronted with a sudden pressure dip and worse local gangrene than anticipated, Miyama didn't freeze for a millisecond; if anything, her cadence grew calmer and sharper, without the faintest impulse to hand off the call.
nodes.s10b_007: "Honjo, Poole suction first—let's evacuate all free turbid bile from the subhepatic space right now to cut toxin absorption! Ange, step up crystalloid infusion and call out our ten-minute mean arterial pressure trend every three minutes! Sakaguchi, pack off the transverse colon and duodenum with warm saline laparotomy pads and hold the subhepatic field wide open for me!"
nodes.s10b_008: "Got it—bowel is padded and walled off, subhepatic space fully exposed."
nodes.s10b_009: As the foul pericholecystic bile was rapidly suctioned clear and fluid resuscitation caught up, the blood pressure readout on the monitor steadily climbed back above the safety threshold.
nodes.s10c_001: The truly treacherous part lay right ahead—driven by acute suppuration and perforation, the tissues around the gallbladder neck and Calot's triangle were fiercely engorged and edematous, blurring every anatomical plane into a single swollen mass where one careless slip could injure the common bile duct or tear an artery.
nodes.s10c_002: Pausing with atraumatic dissecting forceps at the margin of Hartmann's pouch, Miyama resisted rushing blindly in.
nodes.s10c_003: Holding the liver-edge retractor steady with his left hand, Sakaguchi angled a laparotomy pad with his right to draw the duodenum gently inferomedially—putting clean, measured counter-traction across the lateral border of Hartmann's pouch without ever overstepping to make her cut for her.
nodes.s10c_004: "I've got traction tension controlled. Deep-plane edema is heavy—opening the lateral plane right along the gallbladder wall first will be safer."
nodes.s10c_005: Studying the swollen triangle intently, Miyama gave a calm nod:
nodes.s10c_006: "That angle is spot-on—hold it right there. The triangle is too densely edematous to tunnel blindly deep; I'll take it fundus-first down the cystic plate toward the infundibulum and isolate every structure entering the gallbladder beyond doubt before clamping."
nodes.s10c_007: Using a fine suction tip to clear blood-tinged ooze off the edematous serosa, Sakaguchi gently swept back the loose superficial fibrinous veil, bringing the inferior margin of the pouch cleanly into focus.
nodes.s10c_008: "Surface ooze is clear. With edema this heavy, let's methodically define the lower pouch border and cystic-plate plane before committing."
nodes.s10c_010: "My thoughts exactly. Surface landmarks alone aren't safe enough—I'll hug the gallbladder wall with fundus-first dissection to mobilize the pouch cleanly, and nothing gets divided until the two sole structures entering the gallbladder are unmistakable."
nodes.s10c_011: Miyama refused to rush or cut blind.
nodes.s10c_012: Hugging the gallbladder wall patiently through edematous adhesions, she mobilized the specimen step by step from fundus down to infundibulum off the cystic plate, cross-checking repeatedly with Sakaguchi across the table that the common bile duct lay safely shielded deep out of harm's way and that the cystic duct and cystic artery alone stood fully isolated—only then clamping, doubly ligating, and dividing.
nodes.s10c_013: Lifted free intact, the gangrenous perforated gallbladder was placed into the contaminated specimen basin held out by Moe Honjo, after which Miyama secured every pinpoint ooze on the liver bed with electrocautery and warm saline pads.
nodes.s10c_014: Sayaka Nanjo (letting out a quiet breath beside them):
nodes.s10c_015: "Phew—that's the nastiest gangrenous source cleanly out of the way."
nodes.s10d_001: With the septic source resected, Miyama carried out measured, targeted warm-saline irrigation and suction across the right subhepatic space and gallbladder fossa until the aspirate ran completely clear.
nodes.s10d_002: "Blood pressure is back up to one-ten over seventy, heart rate down to ninety-two, oxygen saturation ninety-nine! Vital trends are rock-steady!"
nodes.s10d_003: "Dr. Miyama, subhepatic irrigation return is clear—I have the silicone abdominal drain and closure sutures ready tableside."
nodes.s10d_004: Under routine protocol for a localized gallbladder perforation, placing a subhepatic drain and calling instrument count for closure would be the natural next step.
nodes.s10d_005: Yet standing at the primary spot with suction tip in hand, Miyama let her eyes linger on the peritoneal reflection lateral to the hepatic flexure of the colon—and abruptly stilled.
nodes.s10d_006: Instead of calling for the drain, she knitted her brows faintly, glanced up at the pre-op contrast CT on the lightbox, and looked back down into the freshly irrigated right subhepatic space.
nodes.s10d_007: "Miyama? What is it—still seeing ooze on the liver bed?"
nodes.s10d_008: "The liver bed is bone-dry and the stump isn't leaking bile. It's just... Sakaguchi, doesn't the total volume of bile we suctioned out of the subhepatic space on entry strike you as a little short?"
nodes.s10e_001: The operating room fell quiet for a beat; even Sayaka Nanjo, halfway through shifting retractors for closure, turned her eyes back into the field.
nodes.s10e_002: Through a sterile gauze pad, Miyama tapped lightly toward the lateral margin of the hepatic flexure toward the lower outer corner of the incision, her tone completely free of emotional impulse:
nodes.s10e_003: "Back in the ER, this gallbladder was under extreme tension, and the specimen we just took out was already more than half decompressed with its perforation pointing straight inferolaterally—yet all the walled-off subhepatic bile we aspirated on entry barely added up to thirty milliliters."
nodes.s10e_004: Sakaguchi immediately recalled that subtle detail on the lightbox before skin incision.
nodes.s10e_005: "You're thinking of that faint, artifact-like low-attenuation streak along the edge of the right paracolic gutter on the pre-op CT?"
nodes.s10e_006: "Exactly. Looking at that streak alone pre-op couldn't prove whether it was real, but once you put the perforation vector together with the missing bile volume in front of us, writing it off as artifact isn't good enough—we need to verify it with our own eyes."
nodes.s10e_007: Looking down into the tidy subhepatic field, Sakaguchi asked seriously:
nodes.s10e_008: "The decompression volume and what we aspirated definitely don't add up. Are you planning to explore further down?"
nodes.s10e_009: "I'm not going on an aimless full-abdominal fishing expedition, nor am I sloshing wash into a clean left abdomen to spread contamination—but that pre-op CT already showed a suspicious fluid wisp down the right paracolic gutter right along the perforation's path, so a targeted look is warranted."
nodes.s10e_010: Lifting her eyes to meet Sakaguchi's across the table, Miyama spoke quietly yet with unmistakable conviction:
nodes.s10e_011: "We can't close after washing the subhepatic space alone. Between the perforation angle, the missing exudate volume, and that suspicious fluid wisp pre-op, whether or not a pocket is hiding down there, the objective evidence more than justifies a targeted check along the right paracolic gutter."
nodes.s10e_013: This time, it was neither the anxious 'I can't prove she's fine' of the safety-pin case nor blind momentum behind a mismatched wristband.
nodes.s10e_014: Meeting his gaze squarely, Miyama didn't waver for half a second:
nodes.s10e_016: "All right—then let's see it clearly. Sayaka, steady the upper retractor for me while I gently sweep the omentum medial off the upper ascending colon."
nodes.s10e_017: Applying smooth, measured traction alongside Miyama down the inferolateral corner of the incision, Sakaguchi gently peeled back a fold of greater omentum tacked down by fibrin along the right paracolic gutter.
nodes.s10e_018: The next instant, an occult forty-to-fifty-milliliter pocket brimming with yellow-green bilious flocculent fluid lay starkly exposed beneath the dazzling surgical lamps—had they cut corners and closed right then, leaving that contaminated collection tucked behind the omental fold would almost certainly have bred a stubborn postoperative abscess.
nodes.s10e_019: Beside the instrument stand, Moe Honjo drew a quiet gasp behind her mask:
nodes.s10e_021: Her expression sharpening at once, Sayaka Nanjo braced the upper retractor rock-steady:
nodes.s10e_022: "Tucked away nasty and deep, too. Pass the long suction tip in—I'll keep the bowel loops shielded."
nodes.s10e_023: Never easing her focus above her mask by a fraction, Miyama guided the long suction tip down to evacuate the hidden pocket completely, then carried out localized warm-saline irrigation and aspiration strictly confined to that contaminated gutter so nothing spilled toward the clean mid- and lower-abdominal bowel.
nodes.s10f_001: Once the last fleck of bilious fibrin was cleared from the paracolic gutter, Miyama returned to the gallbladder bed and cystic-duct stump, pressing a fresh dry gauze sponge gently against them for ten full seconds before lifting it back to inspect—pure white and dry, without a trace of active ooze or subtle bile leak.
nodes.s10f_002: Positioning silicone closed-suction drains neatly near the foramen of Winslow in the right subhepatic space and along the freshly cleared lateral hepatic-flexure gutter, she brought them out through separate right-flank stab incisions and sutured them securely in place.
nodes.s10f_003: "Primary septic source and both contaminated spaces are fully controlled, with zero spillover into the mid or lower abdomen. Ange, Honjo—initiate pre-closure count."
nodes.s10f_004: "Laparotomy pads, small sponges, needles, and instruments counted and verified twice—all counts correct!"
nodes.s10f_005: "Blood pressure one-fourteen over seventy-two, heart rate eighty-four, core temperature starting down, urine output brisk!"
nodes.s10f_006: Letting out a long, quiet breath, Miyama accepted the needle holder from Moe and worked stitch for stitch in seamless rhythm with Sakaguchi across the table, closing peritoneum, musculoaponeurotic fascia, and skin cleanly layer by layer.
nodes.s10f_007: There was no miraculous intervention by any 'God of the Operating Room'—only evidence, anatomy, and unsparingly rigorous judgment. As the final sterile dressing was smoothed neatly across the patient's right upper quadrant, the demanding emergency procedure came steadily to rest.
nodes.s11_001: Even after the sterile drapes came down, Miyama was in no hurry to go change; instead, she stayed right beside Sakaguchi to oversee the patient's smooth transfer onto the recovery gurney, handing off drain-output watch points, antibiotic redosing times, and repeat-lab intervals item by item in person to the post-op nursing team.
nodes.s11_002: Just as the handoff wrapped up, the patient's eyelashes fluttered on the recovery gurney as she drifted awake from general anesthesia. After answering her name and noting mild fullness over her right upper abdominal incision on cue, the still-groggy woman blinked up at Sakaguchi beside the bed, then over at Miyama wrapped collar-to-cuff in her dark-green sterile surgical gown, and ventured hesitantly:
nodes.s11_003: "...Thank you both so much, Doctors... Um, Dr. Sakaguchi, could I ask a slightly weird question while you're here...?"
nodes.s11_005: "Nothing hurts, really... it's just, right before I fell asleep on the operating table earlier, I could've sworn I saw a woman with no clothes on—wearing nothing but a cap and a mask—come running into the operating room... Was that a hallucination from my high fever and the anesthesia?"
nodes.s11_006: Above their surgical masks, Sakaguchi and Miyama traded a completely deadpan, unspoken glance.
nodes.s11_007: Miyama's brow tensed by a millimeter for half a beat as her eyes stayed fixed squarely on the post-op chart clipboard in her hands; stifling the amusement in his eyes, Sakaguchi steered the subject smoothly with an utterly straight face:
nodes.s11_008: "Acute gallbladder perforation with high fever very commonly causes brief perceptual fuzziness right around anesthesia induction. The source of infection has been completely cleared out, so you don't need to worry about another thing tonight."
nodes.s11_009: Kaori Miyama (her tone impeccably prim and earnest):
nodes.s11_010: "Precisely. Your temperature, heart rate, and oxygen saturation are all right where we want them; your sole priority tonight is resting flat, minding the drain lines so they aren't tugged, and focusing on recovery rather than dwelling on pre-anesthesia imagery."
nodes.s11_011: Kasumi Asou (blinking twice, looking even more baffled than before):
nodes.s11_012: "...Was it really just the anesthesia playing tricks? Because the second this doctor spoke just now, even her voice sounded identical to the woman in my hallucination... Modern anesthetics really are something else..."
nodes.s11_013: Only after seeing for themselves that the patient was conversing comfortably with rock-steady recovery curves did the two of them finally head to the locker rooms to shed their sterile gowns.
nodes.s11_014: At 7:25 p.m., stepping out of the locker corridor in a crisp, dry set of scrubs, Miyama paused by the surgical-suite hallway wall, rested her shoulders lightly against the cool paneling, and finally let out a long, genuine sigh of relief.
nodes.s11_015: Walking out just after filing the instrument count sheet, Moe Honjo approached holding a neatly squared paper bag in both hands and held it out with flushed cheeks.
nodes.s11_016: "Great work today, Dr. Miyama! Here are your personal clothes from OR #3 earlier—I folded everything neatly into this bag for you... Um, now that the patient is safely settled in recovery, may I offer one tiny reminder?"
nodes.s11_017: Taking the paper bag, Miyama arched an eyebrow:
nodes.s11_019: "Next time you decide to run a variable-elimination experiment... please, please put scrubs on before entering the surgical suite!"
nodes.s11_020: The corner of Miyama's mouth twitched faintly, though she gripped the paper bag without batting an eye:
nodes.s11_021: "Rest assured, there won't be any repeat of that experimental variable."
nodes.s11_022: Swallowing a giggle, Moe gave a polite bow and headed off to send the trays down to central sterile. Standing nearby as Miyama held her bag of casual clothes, Sakaguchi asked offhandedly:
nodes.s11_023: "So—did the 'God of the Operating Room' accept your explanation in person today?"
nodes.s11_024: Shooting him a sidelong look entirely cleared of the heavy fog of recent days, Miyama answered crisply:
nodes.s11_025: "No. Both the prior working hypothesis and experimental design were fundamentally flawed—there's nothing of the sort in an operating room."
nodes.s11_026: "Oh? And here I thought the esteemed Dr. Miyama was getting ready to write up a paper on the subject."
nodes.s11_027: Carrying the freshly delivered post-op brief down the corridor, Asuka Shiromiya came to a stop before her old classmate with a teasing glint in her eyes (the hallway was now clear of outsiders, leaving just the two of them and Sakaguchi).
nodes.s11_028: "Well then, Kaori? That 'statistical clustering anomaly' you argued in my office this afternoon—does it still hold up?"
nodes.s11_029: Meeting her old friend's playful gaze, Miyama lifted her chin with deadpan composure:
nodes.s11_030: "Valid sample size is now three. Conclusion updated—the original hypothesis does not hold."
nodes.s11_031: Asuka couldn't help letting out a quiet laugh. Once her amusement settled, she took in her best friend's newly steadied bearing, dropped her official Director cadence, and spoke warmly and plainly:
nodes.s11_032: "Sayaka mentioned at handoff just now that you caught and cleared that hidden collection down the paracolic gutter before closing. Neither of us is going to pretend those first two cases never happened—you'll make mistakes, and so will I, but that and whether you know how to be a good surgeon have always been two separate things."
nodes.s11_033: Listening quietly for half a beat, Miyama let her gaze drop to the corner of an administrative spreadsheet peeking out of Asuka's white-coat pocket and lobbed a dry counterpunch right back:
nodes.s11_034: "Duly noted on the pep talk. Though before Director Shiromiya wraps up her executive summary for an old classmate, care to confess whether that dinner bento delivered to your desk at dusk is still sitting stone-cold underneath your folders?"
nodes.s11_036: "...How did you know I haven't eaten yet?"
nodes.s11_037: "Because Ange mentioned in passing during her report that the Director's office lights never went off. Spare me the lecture from a fellow workaholic and go heat up your dinner—otherwise you won't need me staging an exorcism before Head Nurse Ishigami marches up to haul you out herself."
nodes.s11_038: "...Barely back on your feet and you're already wielding Ishigami against me! Fine, fine, I'm going back to eat right now. You two worked flat-out all evening—get changed and head home early for some rest!"
nodes.s11_039: Watching Asuka wave with a laugh as she headed down the hall, Miyama glanced down at the paper bag in her hand and turned to Sakaguchi:
nodes.s11_040: "Give me five minutes to change back into my street clothes—walk out together?"
nodes.s11_041: "Sure. I'll wait for you by the main lobby doors downstairs."
nodes.s12_001: At 8:10 p.m., a cool night breeze drifted down the tree-lined street outside Hoshimi Hospital.
nodes.s12_002: Warm white light spilled across the pavement from the glass storefront of a 24-hour corner convenience store, carrying a faint curl of oden broth steam past shelves half-cleared of discounted evening bentos; in the distance along the elevated tracks, a passing commuter train rumbled softly through the night.
nodes.s12_003: Side by side beneath the glow of the streetlamps, Sakaguchi and Miyama walked at an unhurried pace toward the train station.
nodes.s12_004: Just past the first crosswalk, Miyama—who had been looking quietly ahead down the sidewalk—suddenly spoke up.
nodes.s12_007: "Back at the scrub sinks outside OR #2 earlier this evening—why didn't you take over primary when I offered?"
nodes.s12_008: Tilting her head slightly to look at him, she caught the warm streetlight across her poised profile.
nodes.s12_009: "I explicitly told you or Sayaka to step in for me. Purely in terms of open biliary mileage, taking the knife yourself would've been far less trouble than standing across the table assisting me."
nodes.s12_010: Hands tucked into his coat pockets, Sakaguchi kept an easy, unhurried stride, his tone completely matter-of-fact without a trace of forced theatrics.
nodes.s12_011: "I heard you ask to swap out—I just didn't agree. That case was yours from the start: from the moment Ange burst in with word, closing the patient-ID loop, reading the perforation on CT, pacing resuscitation, and calling the trays were all nailed down firsthand by you, and you had every qualification to see it through. With the primary surgeon already in place, my job was naturally to handle first assistant right."
nodes.s12_012: Miyama's stride slowed by half a beat.
nodes.s12_013: Studying the composed man walking beside her, she fell silent for two seconds before the faintest curve—part quiet pride, part genuine relief—touched her lips.
nodes.s12_014: "...Last week after the mix-up with Ms. Katagiri wrapped up, I thanked you because when everything went sideways, you didn't walk off and leave me holding the mess alone."
nodes.s12_015: Drawing a quiet breath of crisp night air, her voice softened a shade from its usual briskness while remaining clear and candid:
nodes.s12_016: "Tonight was different, though. Right when even I was starting to doubt whether my own judgment could still be trusted... you still dared to leave the call on the next table in my hands and stand across from me to shoulder it together."
nodes.s12_017: "And events proved my judgment wasn't off by an inch. That check down the right paracolic gutter before closing—without you tracking the gap between the pre-op films and our aspirate volume, nobody else tonight might have caught it."
nodes.s12_018: A bright spark lit Miyama's eyes at having a fellow surgeon genuinely recognize her clinical rigor, though she still gave a prim little hum.
nodes.s12_019: "I just happened to keep an extra eye on that corner of the pre-op film... Still, your counter-traction across the table really couldn't be faulted."
nodes.s12_020: "Besides, if I'd actually snatched Dr. Miyama's scalpel back there, once you went home, slept it off, and thought it through, you'd definitely be marching up to me chart in hand first thing tomorrow morning."
nodes.s12_021: Coaxed into a quiet laugh, Miyama shot him a sidelong look.
nodes.s12_022: "Am I really that unreasonable in your book? ...All right, fair enough—if you really had swapped me out tonight, I probably wouldn't have slept a wink."
nodes.s12_023: "After all, we weathered both of those first two mix-ups standing across the same table—it's about time we got a patient who genuinely needed surgery so we could see a real case through properly from start to finish."
nodes.s12_024: Blinking faintly, Miyama let her brow smooth out and gave a warm nod.
nodes.s12_025: "True enough. We can't have Director Shiromiya bracing for an incident review every single time the two of us stand at the same operating table."
nodes.s12_026: Fifty meters ahead at the corner, the bright entrance signboard of the train station came into view.
nodes.s12_027: As the night breeze stirred a few fallen leaves along the curb, the two of them slowed their pace. Recalling the surreal scene he had walked in on inside OR #3 that afternoon, Sakaguchi couldn't resist a light tease:
nodes.s12_028: "Come to think of it, when you stretched out on that table in OR #3 this afternoon for your 'empirical elimination,' how on earth did you fall sound asleep in under three minutes? Most people lying on a narrow cold operating table for the first time staring up at a surgical lamp would spend ages tense as a board."
nodes.s12_029: Adjusting her shoulder-bag strap, Miyama paused her fingers ever so slightly.
nodes.s12_030: Looking ahead toward the warm amber canopy lights of the station, she didn't dodge the question, answering instead in an easy, unassuming tone as though mentioning an ordinary old memory in passing:
nodes.s12_031: "I really was short on sleep the past couple of days. And besides... looking up at a surgical lamp from underneath on the table wasn't completely unfamiliar to me. I lay up on one once before."
nodes.s12_032: Mildly surprised, Sakaguchi glanced over at her:
nodes.s12_033: "You were on an operating table before? Did you have surgery for something?"
nodes.s12_034: Giving a light, unhurried shake of her head, Miyama kept a calm and natural expression.
nodes.s12_035: "No. In the end, they didn't operate."
nodes.s12_036: Pausing half a beat without elaborating another word, she kept her eyes on the ticket gates ahead and added lightly:
nodes.s12_037: "I was still a first-year medical student back then... It was a long time ago."
nodes.s12_038: Leaving it right there, she drew her gaze smoothly back and turned toward Sakaguchi again—with neither lingering shadow nor cryptic hesitation, as if brushing past an unremarkable anecdote from her student days.
nodes.s12_039: Together they came to a stop at the steps outside the station entrance.
nodes.s12_040: "I'm taking this westbound train home. Thanks for today, Sakaguchi—both for first-assisting at the table, and for walking out with me."
nodes.s12_041: "Go home and catch up on sleep properly, Dr. Miyama. Just remember to verify patient identity next time you scrub in."
nodes.s12_042: Right before tapping through the ticket gate, Miyama turned back to look down the steps at Sakaguchi, a clear, crisp, lightly wry smile curving her lips:
nodes.s12_043: "Don't worry—see you in emergency tomorrow. I'll triple-check the patient's identity—and as for myself, I'll remember to put my scrubs on before walking into the operating room next time."
nodes.s12_044: Giving Sakaguchi a light wave, she turned and stepped with brisk, steady strides down the warm, brightly lit platform concourse.
